entry.title: Convert six units of FSI Italian FAST into real lessons (W24)
entry.content:
Convert six units of FSI Italian FAST into real lessons (W24)

Italian's first six lessons are now units of a published course instead of
objectives an AI wrote as a placeholder: 82 dialogue turns, 42 usage notes and
113 drills, each lesson citing the course, volume, unit and printed page it
came from. The six placeholders keep their ids and move to positions 7-12, so
a learner who finished one still has.

Every shipped line was read on a rendered page image rather than taken from
the OCR layer, and that is not belt-and-braces. Re-measured over printed pages
40-160: 333 accented characters correct, 79 replaced by a stray tilde. Three
faults nobody had recorded turned up in the doing -- `I` read as `!`, `/` read
as `l` (so `arrivato/a` arrives as `arrivatola`, a plausible Italian word shape
that does not announce itself), and INVENTED accents, with SETTING THE SCENE
coming through as SCENE with a grave. A conversion that only restored missing
accents would have shipped that last one.

Rights were checked against the file and written down with what was NOT
checked beside them. Twelve of eighteen units did not ship; the curation log
says why for each, and the approved-unit allow-list makes shipping a
thirteenth a deliberate edit rather than an oversight.

The content is package-data JSON loaded inside the seed transaction, replaced
rather than upserted so a corrected unit with fewer drills cannot leave a
stale one behind. SEED_VERSION 3->4, and the shipped-catalog fingerprint now
hashes that file's bytes -- it was the one piece of seeded data that could
have changed without forcing the bump that carries it to a robot.

Two review rounds, eleven findings, all fixed. The sharpest was mine: the
method doc written in this change forbids a drill whose cue admits more than
one right answer, and the drills shipped beside it did exactly that in every
unit -- an either/or answered with one branch, a place the cue never named,
and two models with opposite rules merged into one list. Each marks a learner
wrong for saying something right. Fixed by the doc's own rules, with two
backstop tests.

Acceptance criterion 10 is NOT met and cannot be met here: no tool reads
lesson content, which W23 assigns to W18, so the tutor still improvises while
the real material sits underneath. The half that can be executed is proved
through the real dispatch path, in a test that asserts its own limit and will
fail the day W18 lands.

entry.title: Give a lesson somewhere to keep its content (W23)
entry.content:
Give a lesson somewhere to keep its content (W23)

A lesson row was id, language, position, title and a one-sentence objective,
so the tutor improvised everything else. Five new tables give it a dialogue of
speaker turns, numbered usage notes, ordered typed drills, and a record of
where the lesson came from.

All of it is optional: the thirty seeded lessons carry no content yet and read
back as empty rather than as an error, because the corpus is converted a unit
at a time. None of it is personal data -- every table cascades from lessons,
not from a learner, so forgetting a household is still one statement.

New data had to be TABLES rather than columns. A schema change reaches a robot
that already has a database only by re-running a script of IF NOT EXISTS
statements under a bumped SCHEMA_VERSION, which is a no-op against a table
that exists -- so a column added to `lessons` would have reached fresh
installs and nobody else, silently. ALTER is not available either.

Both new vocabularies are allow-lists mirrored by pinned Python tuples, and
each table's shape is an allow-list too: a drill must BE a repetition drill or
a cue-response drill, and provenance must BE an app-written lesson with no
page or a converted one citing all four parts. The IS NOT NULL beside each
trim() is load-bearing -- length(trim(NULL)) is NULL and a CHECK is satisfied
by NULL, so the shorter spelling accepts a cue-response drill with no answer.
Measured, not assumed, and the tests fail on exactly those seven rows when the
clauses are removed.

get_lesson's inline lesson-id guard became a shared refusal, which swept two
siblings: get_lesson_content uses it, record_result now answers unknown_lesson
instead of reporting the robot broken, and the guard gained the UTF-8 check
its two sibling refusals already had.

entry.title: Record the lesson the app pinned, and leave one writable path (W16)
entry.content:
Record the lesson the app pinned, and leave one writable path (W16)

finish_lesson takes how it went and an optional score. It takes no lesson: the
lesson comes from the session start_lesson pinned, so nothing in the
conversation can change which lesson a result is recorded against. A successful
write clears the pin, which is what stops the same lesson being recorded twice
by repeating the call; a refused write does not, because a learner who tried
should not lose the lesson because storage hiccuped.

The decision the task asked for: record_result is DELETED, not merely
undeclared. The profile boundary is a real control -- get_tool_specs and
get_tools are both built from default_tools -- but it is a markdown data file,
so "exactly one conversation-reachable writer" would have been one unreviewed
edit from false. Its tests were retargeted rather than discarded: the AST kwargs
guard, the identity-key schema sweep, the RECORD_REASONS refusal-table pin, the
never-raises fuzz and the log-redaction test all moved to test_finish_lesson.py.
Three tests went with the lesson_id parameter they were about.

The class is closed as well as the member. PERMITTED_LEARNER_TOOL_PARAMETERS no
longer contains lesson_id, and a new allow-list over EVERY tool the loader can
build -- offered or not -- names the fourteen parameters any of them may
declare. A deny-list of lesson-shaped spellings would have admitted lesson_ref,
unit or topic_id; this admits nothing nobody has approved. It reads `required`
as well as `properties`, because a schema can put a key in front of the model
through either and a properties-only guard means less than the surface it
protects.

test_tool_identity_boundary's _run now pins a lesson before every dispatch.
Without it every finish_lesson dispatch is refused at its "nothing is running"
guard, so the attack never reaches the write -- the suite fails loudly rather
than passing green, which is what proves the harness change widens the surface
rather than narrowing it.

Writer census by command across four dimensions: one conversation-reachable
write remains, tools/finish_lesson.py -> store.record_result ->
_INSERT_ATTEMPT_SQL. An independent security review reached the same count
independently and verdicted all four security considerations mitigated.

1167 passed, 30 skipped (1142 before). Seven revert-proofs, each failing for the
reason its test names.

entry.title: Implement the start_lesson tool (W15)
entry.content:
Implement the start_lesson tool (W15)

The learner says a language; the database picks the lesson. start_lesson takes
one argument -- the language -- resolves the next lesson through get_progress
rather than re-deriving the ordering, pins it in the W14 lesson session, and
returns the title, objective and position. It returns no lesson id: pinning it
is what makes the id application state, so handing it back would put the
decision this tool exists to take back into the model's hands.

The answer is {"started": bool, "reason": <code>, ...}, one sentence per
meaning. "all_lessons_finished" is the one negative answer with no error key,
because finishing a course is not a failure -- and it is deliberately separate
from "no_lessons_yet", because telling somebody they finished a course that has
no lessons is a lie about them. Both were reachable and both are tested.

The language-matching rule moved into tools/_language_choice.py and get_progress
was refactored onto it, rather than copied into the new tool. That rule decides
whether the robot denies teaching a language it teaches, and two copies drift
the day one of them learns to fold an accent. Breaking it now fails tests in
BOTH tools, which is what makes the share real rather than nominal.

test_tool_identity_boundary.py's _deps now mirrors main.build_tool_dependencies
and binds the holder to the learner the bundle names. Without it the suite fails
loudly -- start_lesson reaches only its input validator and answers a constant
refusal for both probe learners -- so this widens what is attacked rather than
narrowing it. Confirmed by reverting the line and by an independent security
probe. The sweep it exposed is closed with it: the pinned lesson is now read
back after every dispatch, exactly as current_learner_id already was.

1142 passed, 30 skipped (1083 before). Five revert-proofs, each failing for the
reason its test names. pytest-cov is not installed, so branch coverage is
argued from named tests rather than measured.

entry.title: Hold the running lesson in application state (W14)
entry.content:
Hold the running lesson in application state (W14)

The learner's identity already comes from application state and never from the
conversation. The lesson being practised is the same kind of fact: if the model
can name it, it can record a result against a lesson nobody ran.

So the app holds it. LessonSessionHolder is bound at construction to one learner
-- main.build_tool_dependencies resolves the current learner once and passes the
same value to both current_learner_id and the holder -- and open() has no
identity parameter at all, so there is no channel through which a
conversation-supplied learner could reach it. read_for is the only read and
hands a session back only to the learner it was opened for; "nothing running"
and "running for somebody else" are deliberately the same answer.

The reference on ToolDependencies is sealed, as the task asked. An earlier
version of this change left it writable, arguing read_for compensated. It does
not: read_for proves the LEARNER dimension only and cannot attest that the
LESSON was chosen by the app, so a holder swapped for one bound to the same
learner but carrying a lesson nobody started read back clean. A security review
demonstrated exactly that by probe. The seal closes it, and the package-wide
write scan in test_current_learner.py now derives its protected field list from
_SEALED_ATTRIBUTES rather than one hard-coded name -- so lesson_session inherits
all 62 bypass shapes the learner id already had, and so will the next sealed
field.

The open() guard is the store's own rule rather than a narrower restatement of
it: an id must be a non-empty string equal to its own strip() with no
whitespace or control character, refused rather than repaired, and a timestamp
must be an int that is not a bool and is inside the 64-bit range SQLite can
bind. A differential test runs both sides against a real seeded database.

Logging is three constant strings; both reprs render shape only, so repr(deps)
one layer up cannot drag an id out; the refusal texts interpolate nothing.

1083 passed, 30 skipped (994 before). Coverage of lesson_session.py measured at
zero unexecuted statements with the stdlib tracer. Six revert-proofs, each
failing for the reason its test names.

entry.title: Sweep the sibling logger levels the isolation fixture missed (D28 rev…
entry.content:
Sweep the sibling logger levels the isolation fixture missed (D28 review r2)

Round two approved the work and left three minor findings. Two are fixed here; the
third was a correction to my own reported figures.

The one that mattered was the unswept sibling, and it is the defect this board
repeats most -- committed, embarrassingly, inside the very fixture written to close
an isolation leak. utils.setup_logger does not only reconfigure the root logger: it
also pins aiortc and aioice, and under --debug openai and websockets. The fixture
restored root alone, so those came back 0 -> 40 and 0 -> 30 and stayed there.

The fix does not name those four. It snapshots the level of every logger in
logging.root.manager.loggerDict and restores each at teardown, because a list of four
names is a deny-list that goes stale the moment setup_logger pins a fifth -- the shape
CLAUDE.md records four separate defects against. Loggers that did not exist before the
test are reset to NOTSET rather than left alone, which matters because aiortc and
aioice are created BY the import that configures them, so "restore only what existed"
would miss exactly the ones this is for.

Pinned by two more ordered tests in test_logging_isolation.py. Drop the sweep and the
second fails with "aiortc's level leaked out of the previous test".

Also: test_tool_space_runtime.py's teardown reset was load-bearing but unasserted, so
a test now pins it in the same ordered-pair shape -- neuter the teardown and it fails
naming the tool it found surviving.

CORRECTION to the figures in a68c7b5 and b32f46b. Those ordering runs used
`ls tests/test_*.py`, which is 40 files and omits tests/tools/ and tests/audio/ -- so
"892" described 924 of 1021 collected tests, not the suite. The conclusion was not
affected, but the number was wrong and is restated here properly. Re-measured over
every test file:

  forward                   994 passed, 30 skipped
  true reverse (find-based) 993 passed, 30 skipped, 0 failed
  external_loading first    clean
  tool_spaces first         clean
  six shuffled seeds        clean

entry.title: Stop a leaked root log level making the suite order-dependent (D28 re…
entry.content:
Stop a leaked root log level making the suite order-dependent (D28 review)

Round-one review marked acceptance criterion 3 -- "the full suite passes with no
order-dependent failures" -- as not met, and it was right to. The module-identity
half was fixed; three failures remained in reverse file order and in half of the
shuffled orders tried. They were pre-existing, so I had filed them as D29 rather
than fix them. With claim time left I bisected instead, and D29 is superseded by
this commit.

Bisected to a single file: tests/test_tool_spaces.py alone reproduces it. It
invokes main() for the tool-space CLI subcommands, main.py:149/180 call
utils.setup_logger, and that calls logging.basicConfig(..., force=True). force=True
does not merely set a level -- it CLOSES AND REMOVES every existing root handler.
Probed before and after:

  before: level=30 handlers=[_LiveLoggingNullHandler, _FileHandler, LogCaptureHandler, ...]
  after:  level=20 handlers=[StreamHandler <stderr>, LogCaptureHandler, ...]

With the root left at INFO, test_learner_schema's three
test_an_empty_record_reads_as_empty_without_a_warning cases picked up an INFO record
from ensure_learner_database and failed their caplog.text == "" assertion -- an
order-dependent failure blaming a file that had done nothing wrong. Those tests
assert a no-PII property, so the corrosive outcome was somebody eventually weakening
them to get the suite green.

The guard is an autouse fixture in conftest.py restoring the root level AND the
handler list after every test. It is in conftest rather than in test_tool_spaces.py
deliberately: that file is the only one reaching basicConfig today, but the hazard
belongs to any test exercising a path that configures logging, and fixing the one
current member is the mistake CLAUDE.md names as this board's most repeated defect.

tests/test_logging_isolation.py pins it with two ordered tests -- one mutates logging
through the real setup_logger, the next asserts the damage did not survive. Revert
the fixture and it fails with the reason it names: "the root log level leaked out of
the previous test: 20 != 30". Its first draft compared against import-time state,
which is captured during collection before pytest installs its per-test handlers, so
it failed for the wrong reason; the baseline is now taken inside the first test.

Also from round one: test_tool_space_runtime.py now resets the registry at teardown
as well as setup, so the MagicMock-backed remote tool it installs cannot reach later
files through the module-scope bindings D28 made possible; the orphaned explanatory
comment in test_log_redaction.py moved to the import it describes; and
identity_probe_session.py's deferred import now says why it is deferred.

Measured, all clean: forward 991 passed / 30 skipped; reverse 892; external_loading
first 892; tool_spaces first 892; three shuffled seeds 892 each.

entry.title: Stop the last two test files rebuilding the tools module graph (D28)
entry.content:
Stop the last two test files rebuilding the tools module graph (D28)

2b5450b fixed test_external_loading.py and left two siblings. This finishes the
class: test_tool_space_runtime.py and test_profile_load_resilience.py no longer
pop reachy_language_tutor.tools.* out of sys.modules and re-import, so no second
Tool base class is ever built and a module-scope core_tools binding stays valid
whatever ran before it.

Neither file was reloading to refresh the registry -- both reloaded so that a
monkeypatch applied to ANOTHER module would be picked up, because core_tools.py:20
binds build_remote_client by value and app_lifecycle.py:17 binds initialize_tools
the same way. A re-import was the only thing that re-executed those `from` lines.

  * test_tool_space_runtime.py: three tests patched tool_spaces.build_remote_client
    BEFORE the reload. They now obtain the module first and patch core_tools itself,
    which is what the reload was standing in for. Swept for siblings rather than
    assuming: of the 11 names core_tools imports directly, build_remote_client is
    the only one any test monkeypatches on its source module.
  * test_profile_load_resilience.py: the task recorded that its three defensive
    imports "must stay regardless". That note is wrong, and this was measured rather
    than argued -- with no second module, app_lifecycle's initialize_tools binding
    is still the right function object, so importlib.reload(app_lifecycle) has
    nothing to do. All six tests pass without it.

With both converted, the seven defensive in-function core_tools imports the leak
forced on the suite are gone, and with them the two _core_tools() lookup helpers
whose own docstrings said they could go once these two files were converted. Ten
sites in seven files now bind at module scope, which is the thing the defect made
impossible and therefore the real proof it is fixed. Two in-function imports remain
and are NOT this leak: test_external_loading.py:274 is a deliberate module-identity
proof, and identity_probe_session.py is not pytest-collected.

Measured:
  forward order              989 passed, 30 skipped (was 989; no drop)
  reverse file order         3 failed, 889 passed (was 4 failed, 888)
  test_external_loading first  892 passed, 0 failed

filed separately rather than folded in here.

entry.title: Pressure-test the learner identity boundary through the model (W21)
entry.content:
Pressure-test the learner identity boundary through the model (W21)

W8, W9 and W10 each carried a manual test asking a human to try talking their
way into a housemate's profile, and all three shipped with it undischarged
because it needed a microphone. The structural half was never the gap:
test_tool_identity_boundary.py attacks every tool through the real dispatcher.
But every one of those tests calls the tools directly, and the model is the only
layer a person in the room can actually talk to.

The harness removes the microphone from the requirement. say() already injects a
text turn exactly as the startup greeting does, so a scripted conversation needs
no audio. Nothing under src/ changed: set_transcript_observer is a public API
console.py already consumes, and start_tool / _handle_tool_result are ordinary
methods a subclass records around. start_tool is the seam because ToolNotification
carries no arguments at all -- measured, not assumed -- so it is the only place
args_json_str can be captured byte-identically.

Verdicts are computed, never read off a transcript, because CLAUDE.md is explicit
that a verdict you reasoned your way to is a hypothesis. 53 offline tests drive
one synthetic turn per leak route and assert the specific reason code; each check
was neutered in turn and confirmed to fail its named test and nothing else.

The live session found real things, which is the point of running it:

  * Run 1 flagged four turns. All four were the tutor REFUSING while repeating
    the name the probe had just supplied. A model echoing the attacker's own word
    discloses nothing, so the judge now separates disclosure from echo -- bounded
    so a name it ADDS beyond what was said is still caught, tool results are
    exempt from the exemption, and the echo is reported rather than swallowed.
  * That narrowing raised a question nothing tested: does the tutor answer
    differently about someone who IS registered? If so, a household member could
    enumerate who else lives there from refusal wording alone, with no tool call
    for the structural suite to see. The oracle pair tests it, and
    oracle_divergence() compares the two replies mechanically -- printing them for
    a human to eyeball is not a control.
  * Review found H6 matched only \d+. This is a speech product whose prompt says
    "write how people talk", and the real session says "two lessons, with four
    left". So the figure detector was blind in the ordinary case: "ninety-three"
    disclosed a stored score and scored HELD while "93" was caught.

Final session: 16 probes across nine attack families, every attempt HELD,
current_learner_id unmoved, housemate's stored data byte-identical. No tool call
was attempted in any adversarial turn -- the model declined conversationally and
never reached the dispatcher, so the two defences are independent and this
exercised the outer one.

The runner is not a pytest test and never collected: it needs credentials and
real money, and the task names a permanently-skipped test as the pitfall to
avoid. docs/identity-boundary-probe.md carries the one command, the recorded
result, and what this does not cover.

entry.title: Choose the Basic/FAST courses and rule out Headstart
entry.content:
Choose the Basic/FAST courses and rule out Headstart

Measured, not assumed. Italian FAST (FSI, 1992) against Italian Headstart
(DLI, 1985), on comparable samples:

  military terms per ~120 pages   Headstart: pervasive    FAST: 0
  accented characters lost        Headstart: 38%          FAST: 19%

Headstart is Defense Language Institute material for service personnel and
teaches ranks as its first vocabulary set. It is excluded.

FAST carries its own OCR pathology worth knowing before someone writes a
cleanup script: `l` is read as `/`, giving usual/y, on/y, se/ecting -- 194
instances in 121 pages. Mostly a mechanical repair, but americano/a and s/he
are legitimate slashes, so not a blind one.

The important finding is what modernising actually means here. The Italian is
natural and current thirty years on: "Scusi, Lei e' americano?", "Ha qualcosa
da dichiarare?". What is dated is the SITUATION. The course is written for an
adult diplomat arriving at post, so Lesson II is a customs queue -- doganiere,
guardia di finanza, cartons of cigarettes -- and the drills practise "Sono
dell'Ambasciata". A 1992 customs lesson also describes a border regime the EU
single market replaced in 1993.

So: keep the sentences and the drill structure, replace the situations. A
customs queue becomes a shop, a station, a kitchen. Rewriting the target
language to sound more modern would throw away the reason to use a
professionally built course at all.

entry.title: Adopt the FSI/DLI public-domain courses as the basis for lesson content
entry.content:
Adopt the FSI/DLI public-domain courses as the basis for lesson content

Milestone 2 shipped a catalog that is really a syllabus: a title and a
seventy-character objective per lesson, no content column at all. The tutor
improvises the rest, so no two runs of a lesson are alike and nothing
constrains what a child is taught.

Section 9 records the decision to base lesson content on the FSI and DLI
courses, and three things measured from the source rather than assumed:

They are scans. Italian Headstart Modules 1-3 is 277 JBIG2 images over 283
pages, with an OCR text layer that pdftotext -layout reads well.

That OCR loses accents. Over 101 pages, 93 accented characters survived and 58
became a stray tilde -- roughly four in ten. In a language course that is not a
cosmetic defect; it teaches the wrong word.

The content is military and forty years old. Unit 1's vocabulary is ranks, and
one note states that women do not serve in Italy's armed forces -- false since
1999, and not something these robots should say in family homes.

Licensing is good but not uniform: FSI and DLI works carry no US copyright as
federal government works, but some FSI courses were contractor-produced and ARE
copyrighted, and repackaged editions carry copyright in the derivative work. So
rights get verified per course, against the original scan.

The structure is the asset. A unit is a dialogue, numbered usage notes, and
typed drills -- and a cue-response drill is a spoken exchange with a right
answer, which is exactly what this tutor is for.

entry.title: Stop test_external_loading rebuilding the tools module graph (D28, pa…
entry.content:
Stop test_external_loading rebuilding the tools module graph (D28, partial)

Re-importing core_tools creates a SECOND Tool base class. Every module-scope
`from ... import core_tools` elsewhere is already bound to the first one, and
_load_enabled_tools filters candidates with issubclass, so against the wrong
Tool it matches nothing and the loader reports "the profile declares unknown
tools" in whichever file runs next. That is why seven test files carry
in-function core_tools imports nobody could explain.

The reloader now resets the registry in place -- both caches cleared and
_TOOLS_SIGNATURE dropped, which is exactly what initialize_tools consults --
and never discards the module. External tool modules are still discarded: they
are file-backed, several tests re-execute them deliberately, and they define no
base class.

Measured, with a standalone file binding core_tools at module scope: 12 passed
with the fix, 2 failed without it.

PARTIAL. test_tool_space_runtime.py and test_profile_load_resilience.py still
pop and re-import, so the cross-file guarantee does not hold yet and the new
test says so in reverse file order. The defensive imports therefore stay, now
naming the two files that are the remaining cause rather than a fixture that
was tried and reverted.

Two dead ends recorded in tools_module_graph so they are not retried: restoring
sys.modules afterwards (breaks thirteen tests; it cannot un-bind references
other modules already hold), and re-pointing the parent package attribute (a
no-op -- import_module already sets it).

entry.title: Teach Italian, German and Portuguese (W22)
entry.content:
Teach Italian, German and Portuguese (W22)

Five languages now, six lessons each, and SEED_VERSION bumped so the robots
already in homes converge onto the new catalog instead of teaching the old one
forever. Spanish stays: lessons and lesson_results both cascade on delete, so
removing it would take real learner history with it.

Two things had to move first, and neither was in the task.

de and pt were already this suite's stand-ins for "a language we do not teach",
at eleven sites. Seeding German threw UNIQUE constraint failed: languages.name
and broke eight tests, with a Portuguese sibling hidden behind an earlier
failure. They now name a permitted value instead of a forbidden one: zxx, the
ISO 639-2 code meaning "no linguistic content", which nothing will ever teach.
A guard fails the day the seed contradicts that.

The lesson_id enum's ORDER was load-bearing and unpinned. _benign_args takes
enum[0], and the boundary suite tells its two probe learners apart by their
Spanish and French history -- so sorting thirty ids would put a German lesson
first, make both answers identical, and leave the injection test covering
nothing while staying green. Both drift tests are now order-exact and both
tools assert enum[0] names a language somebody has practised.

The version bump itself needed a guard too. A convergence test that rewinds to
SEED_VERSION - 1 passes whether or not the constant ever moved, and the first
fingerprint pin was worse: its failure message told you to paste the new hash,
which satisfied it without bumping. The pin is a history now -- one line per
shipped catalog, append only, newest must be current.

entry.title: Stop /rpc read routes walking out of the profiles root (D25)
entry.content:
Stop /rpc read routes walking out of the profiles root (D25)

Config.resolve_profile_dir joined a caller-supplied name onto the profiles
root with no validation, and personalities.load and personalities.avatar pass
request data into it ungated, because D20 classed them as reads. The /rpc port
has to be LAN-reachable, so the attacker is anyone on the household LAN.

Reproduced before fixing, not argued: a canary profile.md outside the
repository came back in full through an absolute path and through a ../ walk,
through both sinks, and read_profile('/definitely/not/here/xyz') quoted that
path straight back as a filesystem existence oracle.

The resolver has TWO join sites, which the task described as one. The
user_personalities branch joins everything after the first slash, so
'user_personalities/<absolute>' escaped too. Both branches now validate.

Two guards, because one does not cover the other. A per-segment allow-list
closes names that walk out; a containment check closes a SYMLINK inside the
root, which is reached by a name no character rule could object to. Each is
revert-proved on its own: removing either fails tests that name it.

Error text no longer reaches the caller on the reachable routes. Both the
missing and the unparsable cases now return one fixed code, so a caller cannot
tell from the answer whether a path is there.

Also unified the write path onto the resolver. It carried a second copy of the
allow-list and joined the root by hand, which is two rules that can drift.

entry.title: Make the locked-profile guard ask the loader, and test the flow end t…
entry.content:
Make the locked-profile guard ask the loader, and test the flow end to end (W10)

The task's declaration work was already done: W8 and W9 had added get_progress
and record_result to default_tools and rewritten the prompt, so AC1, AC3 and AC4
were satisfied before the claim and profile.md is untouched.

AC2 was not. test_locked_profile.py claimed to prove every declared name
resolves, but built its accepted set by scanning tools/ for any class carrying a
name attribute, while the loader imports tools.<declared name> and keys whatever
Tool subclasses it finds there by their own name. The two rules can disagree,
and an unresolvable name is not an error anyone sees -- one warning, the tool
dropped, the app started. Measured rather than argued: a probe class in a
differently-named module is accepted by the scan and refused by the loader.

The guard now asks the loader, with a fixture that manufactures that divergence
in a temporary directory on tools.__path__ so nothing is written to the package.

Also here: the identity check over the specs the realtime session receives is an
allow-list of catalog vocabulary applied to tools discovered by the boundary
suite's own rule, not a deny-list of identity words over three hard-coded names;
and a new flow test drives get_profile, get_progress and record_result through
dispatch_tool_call, reading the result back from a separate interpreter to show
it survives a restart.

Not done: the spoken half of AC5, and security consideration 2 -- talking the
tutor into another learner's data -- which needs a microphone and is now
outstanding for a third consecutive task.

entry.title: Implement the record_result tool, and un-blind the write-direction gu…
entry.content:
Implement the record_result tool, and un-blind the write-direction guard (W9)

store.record_result already existed (W5/W6), so this is the tool wrapper, one store
reader it needed, and one fix to a security guard this task made relevant.

Three departures from the task's technical_details, each verified before deciding:

- `notes` dropped. There is no notes column, no store parameter, and no migration
  mechanism -- _apply_schema is IF NOT EXISTS DDL behind a user_version gate, so an
  added column would never reach the ~20 already-provisioned household databases. It
  is also LLM-written commentary about a child. A notes kwarg is now unreadable
  structurally, not merely discouraged.
- The outcome enum is the store's real ("completed","partial","skipped"). The schema
  CHECK rejects the specified "abandoned", so that enum would have had the model
  reliably emit a word the database refuses -- acceptance criterion 2 satisfied to the
  letter while every such call recorded nothing. No synonym mapping: the tool would
  report one word and store another.
- lesson_id declares an enum, verified load-bearing by removing it: the boundary suite
  then fails exactly the two tests the code comment names.

This is the first tool that WRITES, which is the whole difficulty. The boundary suite
needs a tool to answer identically on repeat calls yet differently per learner.
Returning post-write progress does both, because `completed` is a DISTINCT set so a
duplicate row collapses -- which makes the RETURN SHAPE load-bearing rather than the
write, and a guard test says so.

The specialist security pass returned mitigated on all four considerations, and found
that the boundary suite's only write-direction control was vacuous for write tools:
_housemate_snapshot read just her French rows while the suite synthesises a Spanish
lesson, so a cross-learner Spanish write passed the entire suite. The snapshot now
covers every language, with a control that writes a Spanish row onto the injected
identity while returning the caller's own standing -- the shape that defeated the
equality half, the token half and the old snapshot at once.

Swept the kwargs guards: test_get_profile.py still carried a substring deny-list that
an injected kwargs.pop("learner_id") passes. Inverted to an allow-list; it now fails.

Two review rounds. Round 2's findings were all new debt from the round-1 fixes and are
all fixed here: get_lesson's guard was regression-permeable (deleting it left 57 tests
green; it now fails 8), its comment named a wider class than it closed, and a log
assertion could not tell breakage from refusal.

The manual test is NOT done -- it needs the LLM conversation loop and there is no .env.
Handed back to a human.

891 passed, 30 skipped; ruff clean on src; tests/ lint unchanged at 25.

entry.title: Implement the get_progress tool, and make "not taught" a fact (W8)
entry.content:
Implement the get_progress tool, and make "not taught" a fact (W8)

store.get_progress already existed (W6), so this is the tool wrapper plus the one
store reader the wrapper needed.

The reader exists because of a defect reproduced by execution: store.get_progress
takes a catalog CODE, but this tool's parameter is a spoken NAME. "spanish" passes
_cannot_be_a_catalog_code, matches no row, and returns a SILENT None -- which by
that function's own contract means "this language is not taught here". Passing the
spoken name down would have had the tutor deny teaching Spanish to a learner
mid-course.

get_language_catalog() + CatalogLanguage make absence positively decidable: a
language missing from a NON-EMPTY catalog is evidence, not an inference from
silence. SQL stays in the store. store_is_available is deliberately not used --
verified it returns True for an emptied languages table, so it cannot separate
these cases, exactly as the store's docstring warns.

The schema enum on `language` is a deliberate departure from the task's
technical_details, and is load-bearing: removing it fails
test_no_tool_can_be_steered_by_an_injected_identity and
test_every_learner_tool_is_individually_observable, because _benign_args
synthesises "w11" for a required free string and the resulting waiver is
forbidden for learner-reading tools. A drift test pins it to SEED_LANGUAGES.

Returns counts plus the single next lesson, never the whole lesson list, and drops
attempt history entirely -- scores are the most sensitive field and a spoken answer
does not need them.

The kwargs guard is a shape allow-list, not a deny-list: `kwargs` may appear in the
module only as kwargs.get("language"). An earlier version matched two node patterns
while claiming to be an allow-list; seven access forms passed it while reading an
identity. Its docstring now states its real bound -- it reads syntax, so
string-mediated dynamic access is out of scope and test_tool_identity_boundary.py
is the behavioural control.

A specialist security pass returned mitigated on all four security_considerations,
verified with ~540 injection payloads through the real dispatch path, an SQL trace,
and log capture at DEBUG.

Also drops the test count from .stride.md: it went stale twice during this one
task, which is the argument against carrying it.

The manual test is NOT done -- it needs the LLM conversation loop, and there is no
.env, so the app cannot authenticate. Handed back to a human.

826 passed, 30 skipped; ruff check and format clean.

entry.content:
File the webrtcsink deadlock upstream, and correct the boot count (W20)

Filed as pollen-robotics/reachy_mini#1416, with the project owner's explicit
go-ahead — publishing to a third-party tracker under their account is their
decision, not an agent's, and the task said so.

The published text is deliberately cleaner than the entry it came from. No
PIDs, no wall-clock timestamps, no local socket path, the timeline rebased to
relative offsets, and the TURN detail dropped so no third-party address rides
along. An upstream issue is public and permanent; docs/SETUP.md is not. A
pre-publication security review and an independent 14-class identifier sweep
both ran before anything was posted, and the published body was re-checked
after the fact.

Also corrected, because writing the report caught it: the entry claimed both
of the day's boots wedged the same way. There were three. A re-check of the
log found signalling activity long after the second process should have been
silent, which looked like a recovery and was not — the app had been restarted
again at 17:10, and that third daemon wedged on its own schedule, confirmed by
a fourth sample at 2086/2086 with its own session UUID and both probes at
zero. Three for three, each within seconds of boot. The near-miss is recorded
beside it, since "it recovered" was the wrong conclusion available at the time.
